title: Monitoring the Performance of a Balcony-Mounted Photovoltaic System with Battery Storage in Northern Italy
content: This study presents a full year of continuous field monitoring of a balcony-mounted photovoltaic system with battery energy storage (PV-BESS) operating in zero feed-in mode near Parma, Italy. The 1.38 kWp array (60° tilt) was coupled to a 6 kW hybrid inverter and a 2.56 kWh LiFePO₄ battery to shift daytime solar surplus toward the evening demand peak. The system achieved an average annual Self-Sufficiency Ratio (SSR) of 32.3% (55.8% in summer), while zero feed-in curtailment removed 16.4% of the theoretical yield. An unexpected finding, termed the Appliance Paradox, reveals that in deep winter the inverter's standby consumption exceeded the scarce PV yield, turning winter SSR negative (−10.6%). A novel Energy Advantage Index (EAI) is introduced as a PV-BESS design figure of merit, predicting the optimal deactivation window and, prospectively, sizing inverter pairings to avoid the paradox. Economically, a CAPEX of about €1,100 yields a 4.6-year payback and a ten-year ROI of about 137%, improving to 4.3 years and 154% under EAI-driven seasonal control, while cutting the effective cost of electricity by 32% and avoiding 2.35 t CO₂eq over ten years. Balcony PV-BESS systems can meaningfully advance residential energy autonomy, provided inverter sizing and seasonal operation are managed proactively.
